newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: RESEARCH ALERT - PSO seen outperforming.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - PSO seen outperforming.

text.p: Pakistan State Oil (PSO) is seen as one of the most attractive blue chips at the Karachi bourse with earnings growth forecast at 45 percent in 1997/98 (July-June), a research report said on Monday.

PSO's current weakness should prove temporary and the stock is likely to outperform the Karachi Stock Exchange index in 1997, said International Asset Management Company (IAMC) in its quarterly report.
The scrip rose 4.50 rupees, or 1.54 percent, to 296.50 by midday on Monday on turnover of 12,000 shares, dealers said.

State-run PSO is Pakistan's largest oil marketing company, with current market capitalisation exceeding 22 billion rupees, putting it third in the Karachi 100-share index after telecom utility PTCL and Hub Power.
"It controls over 77 percent of the regulated and over 76 percent of the deregulated petroleum products market share in the country," the report said.
The company has given a 30 percent interim dividend.

"We expect the market to re-rate PSO with its full year results announcement in September 1997. Fears of a cash crunch due to high receivables from WAPDA (Water and Power Development Authority) and KESC (Karachi Electric Supply Corporation) have been overdone," it said.

"The recent decline in cash flows due to rising trade debts from government utilities will reverse in 1998 as we expect the government to raise electricity tariffs and improve the payment capabilities of WAPDA and KESC."
For fiscal 1998/99, PSO's earnings growth forecast is seen at around 37 percent, the report said.

"Despite the fact that margins will decline somewhat as PSO moves aggressively into supplying low-margin furnace oil to IPPs (independent power projects), the sheer rise in volume will more than offset the adverse impact on the bottom line," it said.
PSO has signed 10 fuel supply agreements to provide furnace oil to IPPs with a generating capacity of over 2,800 megawatts.
"These new projects are expected to add more than three million tonnes to the current furnace oil volume by 1998, bringing it to over seven million tonnes," IAMC said.
It said a linkage, implemented last June, between local and world fuel prices was also boosting PSO's earnings. "The linkage has dollarised PSO's earnings, hedging it against devaluation."
"PSO's retail outlets are the largest in the business, spanning over 2,600 as against Shell Pakistan and Caltex outlets of 1,121 and 418 respectively," the report said.
